Together, the records document diplomatic consultation, briefing and information-sharing practices, and the handling of politically sensitive material during Brazil’s post-1964 military government.

parsed.core_themes: This folder contains records concerning the acceptance and accreditation of diplomatic and consular representatives, including the recognition of Hugo Vergueiro as Acting Vice Consul of Brazil in Houston, Texas. A September 12, 1963, Department of State acknowledgment granted provisional recognition following a Brazilian government note of August 27 and was addressed to Brazilian Ambassador Roberto de Oliveira Castro. The material reflects formal U.S.–Brazilian procedures for notifying governments of appointments and authorizing representatives to perform consular functions. In this context, acceptability and accreditation encompass official recognition, credentials, and the diplomatic exchange of notes; the folder’s classification also covers letters of credence and exequatur. The records date from before Brazil’s March 1964 military coup and concern the ordinary operation of diplomatic and consular relations between the two governments.
